edges.description: The conserved cereblon-ligase requirement for limb outgrowth and Fgf8 expression, shown in zebrafish and chick, is a route to the limb phenotype that is separate from the human-specific SALL4 degradation. Marked indirect because the intermediates between the ligase defect and the signaling loss are not resolved in the cited work.

edges.description: Impaired cardiac differentiation is the proposed route to the congenital heart malformations seen in affected children; the specific lesions vary.

edges.description: Maternal intake during the 20-36 day window delivers the drug to the embryo at the time of limb, ear, eye and organ formation, which is the initiating step of every branch curated here.

edges.description: The assay reproduces the cardiac and hepatic differentiation arm of the phenotype — thalidomide lowers the cardiomyocyte marker MYH6 and the hepatocyte marker AFP in a dose-dependent manner — in human cells that an animal assay would not flag. It does not model the defining limb lesion, and the neural lineage was spared (PAX6 rose and the neural-rosette marker NESTIN was unchanged), so it captures only part of the syndrome.
edges.limitations: A 2D hiPSC differentiation reads gene-expression biomarkers of cell differentiation, not organ morphogenesis; it contains no limb field, no apical ectodermal ridge, and no vasculature, so the hallmark phocomelia and the antiangiogenic branch are outside it. Marker direction stands in for malformation.
edges.target: Impaired Cardiac and Visceral Organ Differentiation

edges.description: The mouse does not reproduce the disease-defining molecular lesion: thalidomide does not induce SALL4 degradation in rodents, so the limb and organ phenotype is absent.
edges.limitations: This is a true negative with a known cause, not an untested model. Thalidomide degrades SALL4 in humans, primates and rabbits but not in rodents or fish, so a mouse cannot express the mechanism this node asserts; a negative mouse result is therefore not evidence against the human mechanism.
edges.target: CRBN-Dependent Degradation of SALL4 and Developmental Transcription Factors

nodes.description: An older and still-supported account: thalidomide and its breakdown products inhibit angiogenesis and damage the nascent vessels that supply the growing limb and organ fields. In a breakdown-product model, vessels are destroyed within an hour of exposure, before any change in limb signaling-gene expression, which places vascular injury upstream of the signaling loss rather than beside it. Curated as a parallel candidate branch to the cereblon one, and marked indirect.
nodes.id: Antiangiogenic Disruption of the Embryonic Vasculature

evidence.snippet: the theories presently widely supported are thalidomide's antiangiogenic actions

nodes.description: Thalidomide-bound cereblon targets SALL4 and other developmental zinc-finger transcription factors for proteasomal degradation. SALL4 is the load-bearing neosubstrate: heterozygous loss-of-function SALL4 mutations cause a human developmental condition (Duane-radial ray / Okihiro syndrome) that phenocopies the limb, ear, eye and heart defects of thalidomide embryopathy, so depleting SALL4 pharmacologically reproduces the genetic syndrome. The degradation is species-restricted — it occurs in humans, primates and rabbits but not in rodents or fish — which is the mechanistic basis for thalidomide's notorious failure in mouse teratology.
nodes.id: CRBN-Dependent Degradation of SALL4 and Developmental Transcription Factors

animal_models.description: The mouse does not reproduce the disease-defining molecular lesion: thalidomide does not induce SALL4 degradation in rodents, so the limb and organ phenotype is absent.
animal_models.name: Mouse thalidomide exposure

evidence.reference_title: Thalidomide promotes degradation of SALL4, a transcription factor implicated in Duane Radial Ray syndrome.
evidence.snippet: heterozygous loss of function mutations in SALL4 result in a human developmental condition that phenocopies thalidomide-induced birth defects such as absence of thumbs, phocomelia, defects in ear and eye development, and congenital heart disease.

evidence.reference_title: Thalidomide promotes degradation of SALL4, a transcription factor implicated in Duane Radial Ray syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We find that thalidomide induces degradation of SALL4 exclusively in humans, primates, and rabbits, but not in rodents or fish, providing a mechanistic link for the species-specific pathogenesis of thalidomide syndrome.

nodes.description: Thalidomide binds cereblon (CRBN), the substrate-receptor subunit of a CRL4 (CUL4-DDB1) E3 ubiquitin ligase that is required for limb outgrowth and for Fgf8 expression in zebrafish and chick embryos. Binding both inhibits the ligase's normal activity and, as the later substrate work established, reprograms its substrate specificity so that it ubiquitinates neosubstrates it would not otherwise engage. The conserved limb-outgrowth role was shown in fish and chick; the disease-relevant neosubstrate degradation below is not conserved in those species, which is the crux of the model-mismatch.
nodes.id: Cereblon Binding and E3 Ubiquitin Ligase Reprogramming

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a primary target of thalidomide teratogenicity.
evidence.snippet: we identified cereblon (CRBN) as a thalidomide-binding protein. CRBN forms an E3 ubiquitin ligase complex with damaged DNA binding protein 1 (DDB1) and Cul4A that is important for limb outgrowth and expression of the fibroblast growth factor Fgf8 in zebrafish and chicks.

nodes.description: Generalised chronic pain is near-universal in ageing survivors, driven by decades of compensatory loading of malformed and shortened limbs, and is the dominant symptom burden of the adult phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: The health and quality of life of Thalidomide survivors as they age - Evidence from a UK survey.
evidence.snippet: Almost half (49%) of respondents reported generalised pain: 26% said this was severe and/or continuous and a further 23% described it as moderate and/or intermittent.

nodes.description: A spectrum of cardiac malformations; the specific lesions vary and the heart defects are a leading cause of intrauterine and neonatal death in the syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Defects of the heart are likely the cause for many of the intrauterine and post‐natal deaths.

nodes.description: The convergence point of the cereblon and vascular branches at the limb: the limb bud fails to grow out normally and its FGF8 and SHH signaling centers are lost. Because proximal (long-bone) elements are the most affected while the distal hand plate is relatively spared, the characteristic outcome is phocomelia, and the upper limbs are affected more often and earlier than the lower limbs.
nodes.id: Disrupted Limb Bud Outgrowth and FGF8/SHH Signaling

biological_processes: fibroblast growth factor receptor signaling pathway

evidence.snippet: Thalidomide has also been reported to cause loss of FGF and Shh signaling in chick and rabbit embryo limbs and in zebrafish embryos

nodes.description: Thalidomide (and its racemized enantiomers and breakdown products) reaches the embryo during the 20-36 day window, when the limbs, ears, eyes, heart and internal organs are forming. This node exists so that the molecular cereblon branch and the vascular branch below share one parent: they are competing and possibly complementary accounts of one exposure, and the entry does not rank them.
nodes.id: Embryonic Thalidomide Exposure in the Critical Window

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a primary target of thalidomide teratogenicity.
evidence.snippet: thalidomide was widely prescribed to pregnant women as a sedative but was found to be teratogenic, causing multiple birth defects

nodes.description: Beyond the limb, thalidomide disrupts the differentiation of cardiac and visceral (hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal) lineages, consistent with SALL4's role in cardiac and endodermal development. This is the node the ReproTracker human iPSC assay reads out: in that assay thalidomide lowers the cardiomyocyte and hepatocyte differentiation markers while sparing the neural lineage.
nodes.id: Impaired Cardiac and Visceral Organ Differentiation

evidence.reference_title: Animal-free assessment of developmental toxicity: Combining PBPK modeling with the ReproTracker assay.
evidence.snippet: decreased expression of cardiomyocyte-specific marker MYH6 in a dose-dependent manner

It does not model the defining limb lesion, and the neural lineage was spared (PAX6 rose and the neural-rosette marker NESTIN was unchanged), so it captures only part of the syndrome.

nodes.description: Joint replacement for the secondary osteoarthritis of malformed and overused joints, which relieves pain and improves movement despite the abnormal anatomy that complicates the surgery.

evidence.reference_title: Shoulder joint replacement can improve quality of life and outcome in patients with dysmelia: a case series.
evidence.snippet: Patients with dysmelia have acceptable short and mid-term results with resurfacing hemiarthroplasty. It is an effective although somewhat complicated method to relieve pain and improve movement.

nodes.description: Thalidomide taken by a pregnant woman — historically as a sedative and antiemetic for morning sickness, now for leprosy complications and multiple myeloma — reaching the embryo during the sensitive window of roughly 20 to 36 days after fertilization. This is the sole necessary cause: the embryopathy does not occur without the exposure, and a single tablet taken within the window can produce it. The drug both racemizes between enantiomers in body fluids and breaks down into many hydrolytic and hepatic metabolites, so the species that reaches the embryo is a mixture rather than one agent.
nodes.id: Maternal thalidomide intake during the critical window

evidence.snippet: Reports indicate that a single 50 mg tablet of thalidomide during the time‐sensitive window is sufficient to cause birth defects in up to 50% of pregnancies.

nodes.description: Conventional mouse thalidomide-exposure models, which historically failed to reproduce human thalidomide teratogenicity and so reassured regulators that the drug was safe. The failure is now understood mechanistically: thalidomide-bound cereblon does not degrade SALL4 in rodents.

Secondary (acquired) osteoarthritis develops early in the malformed and overused joints of survivors — shoulder, hip and knee — at rates well above the general population, and is the target of the joint-replacement surgery.

evidence.reference_title: Shoulder joint replacement can improve quality of life and outcome in patients with dysmelia: a case series.
evidence.snippet: one third of the respondents are already afflicted with recently diagnosed acquired osteoarthrosis of the shoulder, 58 % are afflicted with shoulder aches

nodes.description: The hallmark limb lesion: severe shortening from reduction or absence of the proximal long bones with the hand or foot plate retained. Predominantly affects the upper limbs.

evidence.snippet: Phocomelia remains the most striking limb deformity caused by thalidomide, and remains the stereotypical image of thalidomide embryopathy.

nodes.description: A human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) biomarker assay in which cells are differentiated toward cardiomyocytes, hepatocytes and neural rosettes while exposed to a compound, and lineage- and cell-specific marker genes (MYH6, AFP, PAX6, NESTIN) are quantified. It classifies thalidomide as a teratogen from the human cells directly, which is what the mouse cannot do. Used here with a pregnancy PBPK model to derive human-equivalent doses; only the in vitro biomarker arm is linked to the pathograph.
